text:
Sam: Heads up — saw 8 pod evictions in eu-west-1 ~11:12 UTC. All GPU inference jobs. Appears tied to a scale-in window. Anyone else seeing this?
Nina: Yup, spikes in our logs. Autoscaler shows scale-down candidates around the same time.
Jordan: Were those pods Guaranteed QoS or BestEffort? Any PDBs blocking binpack?
Sam: Most were Guaranteed with nodeAffinity for `nvidia.com/gpu` (preferred). Kubelet eviction reason in events: 'Evicted by cluster-autoscaler' for drain.
Kevin: We enabled the aggressive consolidation flags last week (`--scale-down-utilization=0.1` + `--scale-down-unneeded-time=1m`) to save cost during low traffic. That could explain premature drains.
autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: scale-down event at 2025-10-22T11:12:18Z — terminated instance i-0a1b2c3d in eu-west-1b, candidate nodes: nid-17f, pods evicted: 8
Nina: Right — I forgot we lowered the threshold. Oops. Can we revert the flag and roll it out slowly?
Jordan: Also noticed some nodes still have taint `gpu-dedicated=true:NoSchedule` and a bunch of GPU pods with `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` affinity. When descheduler isn't active, that leads to fragmentation and then scale-down rips things apart.
Kevin: For short-term mitigation: revert the aggressive flag, increase `--scale-down-unneeded-time`, and add a cooldown window. Long-term we should run descheduler policies after scale events: `RemoveDuplicates` + `LowNodeUtilization` to consolidate GPU pods.
Sam: I'll open a PR to rollback the flag and add a conserved roll-back window. @Kevin can you update CA config and bump the cooldown? @Nina can you schedule a descheduler run after the rollback?
Nina: Yep — scheduling a descheduler job for eu-west tonight and raising the rollout gate. Also adding a quick smoke-check to catch mass-evictions in the next deploy. :thumbsup:
descheduler-bot: descheduler-bot: ad-hoc job queued: "consolidate-post-scale" for eu-west-1 starting in 5m
Jordan: Also consider adding a small eviction-protection label for critical inference jobs (e.g., `rdw:eviction-protect=true`) that the CA ignores during scale-down, or use custom pod disruption budgets for the most latency-sensitive replicas.
Kevin: Agreed. We'll draft a policy: low-traffic consolidation but exempt critical GPU pools + an automated post-scale consolidation step. We'll also add instrumentation to detect 'eviction cascades' and alert earlier.
Sam: Thanks team — priority P1 until we confirm no more spillover during the next scale window. Keep updates here.
